title: Control of heavy metals during the co‐pyrolysis of agricultura/forestry waste with coastal municipal sludge and the adsorption characteristics of recovered modified co‐pyrolytic char toward benzene series VOCs: Combined experimental and simulation study
content:
Abstract

Clean recovery and reuse of solid waste through co-pyrolysis is important to social development. Co-pyrolysis of coastal raw municipal sludge (RS) with three types of agricultural/forestry waste revealed that co-pyrolysis of RS with pine sawdust was the best, with the optimal co-pyrolysis temperature, time and mixing ratio being 850°C, 90 min and 50%, respectively. To further mitigate potential heavy metal contamination, modified sepiolites were synthesized, among which acid/thermally activated sepiolite (TH-SP) demonstrated superior control. The addition of TH-SP increased the absolute solid-phase retention rates of five targeted heavy metals by 22.15% to 42.89%, successfully classifying all heavy metals as low-risk. Consequently, 90% of Cr, Cu, and Pb were converted into relatively stable forms, while the stable proportions of Zn and Cd increased by 10%. Overall, Zn exhibited the highest concentration and Cd posed the greatest potential risk, with solid-phase enrichment following the order of Cr > Zn > Cu/Pb > Cd, and Cu accounting for the largest stable proportion. Furthermore, the adsorption of VOCs by the modified co-pyrolysis char fitted well with pseudo-first-order/Elovich kinetics and Langmuir–Freundlich thermodynamic models. The H-BC-N2 exhibited the best adsorption performance for breakthrough time and adsorption volume, and the adsorption capacity remained at 70% even after six cycles, with physisorption dominating the adsorption process. Simulations of adsorption distance, adsorption energy, and frontier molecular orbitals demonstrated strong heavy metal binding onto TH-SP and excellent VOC adsorption on the modified char. The simulation findings aligned closely with experimental results, confirming the reliability and mechanisms of this process.
